div.div:
pĕdĭtastellus , i, m. dim. peditaster, not in use; formed like parasitaster, etc.; cf.: magistellus, cultellus, etc.,
I.a wretched foot-soldier, tramp: “at peditastelli quia erant, sivi viverent,” Plaut. Mil. 1, 1, 50 Brix ad loc.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
